name: Zohran Mamdani
role: Mayor of New York City (2026–); member of the New York State Assembly (2021–2025)
summary: A Democratic Socialists of America member and Democrat who emphasizes affordability: a rent freeze, fare-free buses, universal child care, a $30 minimum wage and higher taxes on high earners and corporations. He favors a civilian community-safety agency alongside a retained NYPD, sanctuary protections for immigrants, LGBTQ and reproductive rights, and public renewable power. He is a prominent critic of Israeli policy, supporting BDS and ICC warrants, while saying Israel has a right to exist with equal rights for all.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Supports the New York Health Act (single-payer).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Platform calls for a $30 minimum wage by 2030.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Proposes city-run grocery stores, a rent freeze and free buses, implying public provision beats markets in these areas; not stated as a general claim.

public-ownership.rationale: Cosponsored the Build Public Renewables Act (public power authority) and sponsored public-utility bills; no stated stance on rail or all major industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed raising the corporate rate to 11.5% and a 2% surcharge on incomes over $1 million; said he does not think billionaires should exist.

unions-good.rationale: Pledged in his victory speech to stand alongside unions and expand labor protections; backs union labor on public projects.

regulate-corporations.rationale: City banned junk fees and he proposes higher corporate taxes; framing is regulation of corporate behaviour.

cut-welfare.rationale: Record and platform expand public programs (child care, groceries, housing); no support for cuts.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said he does not want more officers and the NYPD's size is appropriate; proposed a civilian Community Safety department and abolishing the Strategic Response Group; kept the commissioner.

rehabilitation.rationale: Committed to closing Rikers, ordered solitary confinement compliance and opened therapeutic housing; appointed a formerly incarcerated corrections commissioner.

abortion-legal.rationale: Backed Proposal 1 (2024) protecting reproductive rights in the state constitution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His sanctuary-city record is about how immigrants are treated, not how many should come; no statement on national immigration levels was found.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Treats climate action as central; cosponsored Build Public Renewables Act; backs All-Electric Buildings Act and congestion pricing.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Reportedly said his focus 'is on outcomes' when reversing on mayoral control, though he calls himself a democratic socialist.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Says Israel has a right to exist 'as a state with equal rights' but declined to support it as a Jewish state, citing religious hierarchy of citizenship.

force-without-un.rationale: Condemned unilateral US strikes on Venezuela and Iran as acts of war.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposed the Astoria gas peaker plant and backed public renewables.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Opposes racism and supports LGBTQ, immigrant and Muslim New Yorkers' equal standing.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Called for ending the occupation of Palestinian territory and opposed Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

corporate-influence.rationale: Speech rejects politics that answers to the few and criticizes billionaires avoiding taxes; lobbying and campaign money not specifically addressed.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Pledged to enforce ICC arrest warrants in city practice.

socialized-care.rationale: Proposes universal public child care; says nothing on housework being socialized.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Strong record of LGBTQ rights support.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said politics should no longer be done to people; proposed co-governance of schools with parent councils.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Backed Proposal 1 on gender identity protections, supports gender-affirming care, created an Office of LGBTQIA+ Affairs.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Himself Muslim; said New York will no longer be a place where one can traffic in Islamophobia and win.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said he does not think there should be billionaires given inequality and rejected politics that answers only to the few.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Backed defunding in a 2020 tweet but as candidate and mayor kept the NYPD and moved away from defund rhetoric; wants Rikers closed but not prisons abolished.

rent-control.rationale: Supports rent control and froze rents on rent-stabilized units (Rent Guidelines Board two-year freeze, 2026).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Commemorated the Armenian genocide in 2026 and condemned the Nagorno-Karabakh expulsions; also calls Gaza a genocide.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Backs fare-free public buses and public renewable power; water and hospitals not addressed.

dense-cities.rationale: Backs increased density near transit and congestion pricing.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Backs unions and his administration reached labor settlements with delivery-app platforms; no explicit statement on bargaining versus individual contracts.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Said he would seek to enforce ICC warrants against Netanyahu and Putin.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Flagship programs (free buses, universal child care) are universal rather than limited to the poorest.

notes: Born October 18, 1991; living. Positions have shifted in office: he reversed his opposition to mayoral control of schools, retreated from 'defund the police' rhetoric, and later dropped some earlier stances (SHSAT). Most evidence on specific issues comes from secondary reports; positions not directly documented are left null.
